description:
## Problem
BenchBox has no TPC-DI metric and its results carry no TPC-DI evidence.

## Owner decisions (choice dialogs, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- Label, exactly: "Derived from TPC-DI. Not an audited TPC result; not comparable to TPC Benchmark Results." (CLI, bundle, site)
- Bundle: "a `benchmark.tpcdi` block holding the generator identity and row counts, per-batch elapsed times, the metric (`th`, `ti1`, `ti2`, `tpc_di_rps`), the audit outcome (status, tests total and OK, failed test names, SQL hash, substitutions), visibility executions, the validity flag and the label. Timed rows are named `TDI_HISTORICAL`, `TDI_INCREMENTAL_1`, `TDI_INCREMENTAL_2`. Result schema takes the next minor version."
- "No compliance class for TPC-DI, plus a rule that TPC-DI never counts as 'official' in the results database."
- "A single-platform TPC-DI cohort may be published as a documented shallow cohort ... The seed workflow regains TPC-DI cells only for platforms that pass the audit."
- Status becomes `experimental`. "No TPC-DI run is published until a DuckDB run passes the full audit."
- 2026-11-21, other phases: "TPC-DI supports only the generate, load and power phases."
- 2026-11-21: generation refuses a scale below 3 ("TPC-DI data generation needs a whole-number scale factor of 3 or more. Got: {sf}."), so a below-floor result can only arrive as a bundle from elsewhere; the validator and admission still refuse it with the reason text.

## Change
Add `core/tpcdi/metric.py` (Clauses 7.5 and 7.6.1): throughputs from DIGen's row counts and the monotonic phase times rounded up to 0.1 second, each incremental time floored at 1800 seconds, TPC_DI_RPS the truncated geometric mean of the historical throughput and the smaller incremental throughput. The result schema takes the next minor version, with the generated JSON schema regenerated, and a `benchmark.tpcdi` block: `source` (provider `digen`, DIGen version, tools archive SHA-256, report and staging manifest hashes, Java version, licence notice shown); row counts RH, RI1, RI2; per-batch elapsed times; `th`, `ti1`, `ti2`, `tpc_di_rps`; `answer_key` (defects found, corrections applied); `etl` (base `databricks-tpc-di@8e0f944`, canonical dialect, SQL hash, the four strategies, rendered modifications, departures kept); `audit` (engine, SQL hash, substitutions, approved modifications, tests total and OK, failed names); `timing` (monotonic times and completion-record times); visibility executions; validity; the under-1800-second flag; the label. Timed rows `TDI_HISTORICAL`, `TDI_INCREMENTAL_1`, `TDI_INCREMENTAL_2`. The builder fills the block from the phases; status stays not validated in this step. Changelog fragment.

## Decision gates
Any field name not in the approved list or this list is shown to the owner and not armed until approved. The schema minor version follows existing convention and is stated in the pull request. The CLI still refuses TPC-DI.

## Verification rubric
Pass: metric unit tests on worked examples, including an update under 1800 seconds and the 0.1-second round-up; `uv run -- python -m benchbox.core.results.bundle_json_schema --check`; a test asserts the block's keys, `source.provider == "digen"`, `etl.base`, the three `TDI_*` rows and the label verbatim on a result built from the milestone fixtures; an older-schema bundle carrying the block is refused; `make pr-preflight` passes; the soundness review of the head is a success.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21)
- The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.
- Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking. `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job the runner never ran or cancelled, never for a failed test.
- Review threads: reply; resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again.
- Subagents are read-only. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment.
- Any limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has not already chosen (see tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120) is shown to the owner before it is committed.
- A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`. One pull request for this item, merged before the next item starts.
- From the quarantine step until the reopening step, no TPC-DI entry point may produce a result that reads PASSED or is admitted for publication.
- Sources. SQL derived from the Databricks project (`src/incremental_batches/**` at commit 8e0f944, treated as MIT on the owner's instruction) may be committed only after the provenance step has merged, only under `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/`, with every file listed in `PROVENANCE.json` and with all comments removed.
- TPC and bankmark files (DIGen, PDGF, dictionaries, configuration, EULA, appendix SQL) come only from the official archive the owner supplies, are committed unmodified and only in the directories named in the tools step. Never copy from the Databricks project or the DuckDB implementation: their copies of the tools or the tools zip, DIGen output, generated reference files, audit snapshots, their copy or rewrite of the appendix SQL, or any generator code (`src/tools/**`). Never commit DIGen output.
- The specification wins over the Databricks project without asking. Each behaviour of the project that is kept and each change made to follow the specification is one row in `benchbox/core/tpcdi/etl/DEPARTURES.yaml`, which the owner approves at the milestone stop.
- A difference from the DuckDB implementation (djouallah/tpcdi) that is not in the written list of expected differences is a finding: it is triaged and listed in the pull request before the step is armed.
- Staging files produced by DIGen are never edited. The official audit, validation and visibility SQL is never edited in the repository.
